rich_summary: Hotravahana explains to a sage that the distressed maiden before them is Amva, eldest daughter of the king of Kasi and his own granddaughter. During the swayamvara of Amva and her sisters Amvika and Amvalika, Bhishma stormed the assembly, defeated the gathered kings, and carried the princesses away to marry his half‑brother Vichitravirya. Amva revealed that she had already chosen King Salwa in her heart, and Bhishma, acknowledging this, allowed her to go. Yet Salwa rejected her, doubting her purity after the abduction. Ashamed to return home and consumed by grief, Amva seeks guidance. The sage Akritavrana suggests either persuading Salwa to accept her or having Parashurama defeat Bhishma. Gradually Amva’s anguish turns toward vengeance against Bhishma. When Parashurama arrives, she falls before him and begs rescue from her suffering.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the mystery of the maiden and reveals her identity as Amva, establishing the personal and familial stakes of the story.
Contains the crucial background: Bhishma’s dramatic abduction of the princesses from their swayamvara, the event that triggers all of Amva’s later suffering.
Encompasses Amva’s tragic arc—her love for Salwa, his rejection, and her humiliation—driving her toward the desire for justice or vengeance.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma storms the swayamvara of the three princesses of Kasi, defeating assembled kings and carrying the maidens away in his chariot.
Amva stands before King Salwa pleading for acceptance while he turns away in suspicion and pride.
In the forest hermitage, the grief‑stricken Amva bows at the feet of Parashurama, tears streaming as she begs for protection.
